newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures end down in lackluster trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures end down in lackluster trade.

text.p: U.S. debt futures ended slightly lower after being thrown on the defensive from this week's quarterly refunding.
Treasury sold $16.0 billion in three-year notes at an average yield of 6.041 percent, in line with estimates of 6.03 percent to 6.04 percent.

More supply is on tap, with Treasury's sale of 10-year notes on Wednesday and 30-year bonds on Thursday rounding out the $38.0 billion refunding. Some traders noted corporate issuance from Raytheon Co expected to hit the market this week, as well.
September Treasury bond futures started the day weak and remained in a tight overall range from 114-10/32 to 114-22/32. Trade was light much of the afternoon.

"It was a non-event," a T-bond futures trader said of Tuesday's action. "I think the 10-year is the key because the 10-year is the most difficult to get through," he said. "If we can get through this one ok then I think the market is going to rally and if it doesn't go well, then I think that sets us up poorly for the 30-year."
Several traders noted that debt futures were able to close in the top half of their daily ranges, despite the supply.

Traders pegged support at the July 22 low of 114-4/32 and at 114-00. The July 22 low was considered significant because it marks the lowest price hit in the wake of semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony. A Eurodollar trader said those levels will likely hold any Wednesday losses and said the market should retrace about two-thirds of its recent slide.
"Most people seem to think we're going to come out of the auctions ok," the trader said.
There was scant reaction to data during the session. U.S. adjusted chain store sales rose 0.3 percent in July versus June, according to Redbook retail sales.
BTM/Schroders reported U.S. chain store sales up 0.5 percent in the August 2 week versus the prior week.
U.S. June housing completions fell 7.8 percent to a 1.282 million unit annual rate. U.S. June leading indicators were unchanged, versus up 0.3 percent in May.
At the close, September T-bonds were down 2/32 to 114-19/32, notes fell 2/32 to 109-22/32, munis fell 1/32 to 120-13/32, Eurodollars fell 0.020 to 94.075.
